proposals.evidence: CDIAL 7733 pattra explicitly gives Lahnda pattar, Punjabi pattā and Bshk. paλ “leaf”. The l/ɬ notation in the latter and regional r-bearing or simple pata forms fit this branch; pana/pan may instead be parṇa. Reviewed comparison: Rana pʌta “leaf” (f_vsg3rhco6pb3m). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

Reviewed comparison: RathwiBareli noṇ “salt” (f_dskpnsiurjtcy). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 7655 pañca explicitly gives Dardic panž/panz and Pashai paĩ/paẽ, alongside Kalasha poñ and Shina poĩ. The survey affricate-to-sibilant and contracted nasal/glide numerals fit this documented five family; exact local phonetic developments remain qualified. Reviewed comparison: Buksa pãntʃ “five” (f_rr5qoqwidwmsw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
